signature.name: George Town UNESCO Zone
signature.detail: The historic core of shophouses, temples and colonial buildings is the reason most visitors come, and it is best explored on foot. Go early in the morning to beat the heat and the crowds.

signature.name: Fort Cornwallis
signature.detail: The star-shaped colonial fort on the waterfront is George Town's most famous landmark and a good starting point for a walk through the old town. Visit in the morning for cooler weather and fewer visitors.

signature.name: Khoo Kongsi
signature.detail: This ornate clan house is one of the most impressive Chinese heritage buildings in the city, with richly decorated halls and carvings. It is a short walk from the old town center; check opening hours before you go.

signature.name: Penang Hill
signature.detail: A funicular ride takes you up for cooler air and sweeping views over the island and city. Go late afternoon to catch the sunset, and expect queues on weekends.

signature.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
signature.detail: A large hillside Buddhist temple complex with a towering statue and pagoda, one of Penang's signature sights. Dress modestly and allow a couple of hours to wander the terraces.

signature.name: Clan Jetties
signature.detail: Traditional stilt villages on the waterfront show a way of life unique to Penang. Walk quietly since people still live here, and go in the morning for softer light.

signature.name: Armenian Street
signature.detail: A charming old-town street lined with heritage shophouses and street art nearby. It is best on foot and early in the day before the tour groups arrive.

signature.name: Pinang Peranakan Mansion
signature.detail: A beautifully restored mansion filled with Peranakan antiques and furnishings, giving a vivid sense of Straits Chinese life. It is an indoor stop, handy during the midday heat.
